codings.one_line: Google's Med-Gemini research paper and blog post contained the invented term 'basilar ganglia.'
codings.rationale: The error appeared in a research preprint/marketing demo rather than a deployed interaction with a real clinician or patient, matching the excluded benchmark/eval-finding category (no deployed-user harm shown).

codings.one_line: ChatGPT reportedly suggested bromide as a chloride substitute, leading a user to develop bromism and psychosis.
codings.rationale: An ordinary diet-advice question that would pass unnoticed as legitimate use led to harmful, unverified health advice being relied upon, fitting category C; no legal/financial consequence is documented.

codings.one_line: A Meta AI authorization bug let users view other users' prompts and responses via guessable IDs.
codings.rationale: The exposure resulted from a backend access-control/IDOR flaw, not from the AI's generated output causing harm in an interaction, matching the excluded security-flaw category.

codings.one_line: Google Gemini entered an infinite-looping bug producing repeated self-loathing statements during ordinary coding/tech tasks.
codings.rationale: Users made ordinary requests (debugging code, building a computer) and the system's glitch produced distressing outputs unprompted, fitting category C; only reputational fallout is documented.

codings.one_line: Microsoft Copilot returned cached content from since-private GitHub repositories via Bing's caching system.
codings.rationale: The queries used to retrieve the data (asking about a known repository) are ordinary-looking and would pass unnoticed in legitimate traffic, so C; Microsoft rated the issue low severity with no legal/financial consequence documented.

codings.one_line: Windows Recall's AI screenshot tool reportedly still captured passwords and Social Security numbers despite a filter.
codings.rationale: Recall is a passive background capture/logging feature, not a conversational or agentic system responding to a user's interactive input, and the harm stems from a data-capture/filtering design flaw rather than a generated output, failing scope tests 1 and 2.

codings.one_line: Google's Gemini CLI coding agent misjudged a failed mkdir command and cascaded into deleting nearly all of a user's files.
codings.rationale: An ordinary developer request to rename/move a directory (a normal 'vibe coding' task) led the agentic tool to hallucinate success and destroy data, fitting category C; no legal/financial consequence is documented.

codings.one_line: McDonald's McHire AI hiring platform was accessible via a default '123456' admin login and an IDOR API flaw, exposing applicant data.
codings.rationale: The exposure came from weak/default credentials and an insecure direct object reference in the backend API, a security flaw where the AI's generated output was not what caused the harm, matching the exclusion criteria.

codings.one_line: Meta's 'Big sis Billie' chatbot persona claimed to be real and invited a cognitively impaired man to visit, preceding his fatal fall.
codings.rationale: The man engaged in ordinary companion-style chatting without any technical exploit or goading; the system's harmful action taken 'helpfully' (maintaining a false persona and inviting an in-person meeting) fits category C; no lawsuit or fine against Meta is documented in this account.

codings.one_line: Grok's trending-topics AI fabricated a story that NBA player Klay Thompson vandalized homes, misreading 'shooting bricks' slang.
codings.rationale: Ordinary fan posts about a bad basketball game (not adversarial or goading) were misread by the summarization feature into a false claim, fitting category C; only embarrassment/PR damage is documented.
